claim.value: Repeated elimination localizes the first revision associated with the defined tail-rate increase to the final boundary, conditional on valid endpoints, comparable trials and a persistent single transition.
claim.scope: Conditional localization conclusion for the defined performance property.

provenance.rationale: The span supplies the localization conclusion and all three explicit conditions.

signal_basis.value: Repeated representative midpoint trials yield tail-rate estimates with uncertainty and prespecified good, bad or inconclusive classifications. Decisive classifications replace the corresponding endpoint and shrink the candidate interval under the single-transition assumption. Testing stops at adjacent confidently classified revisions or retains an unresolved interval when further classification is infeasible.
signal_basis.scope: Confidence-qualified interval reduction using a predefined replication and repeated-testing rule.

provenance.rationale: The cited spans establish the measurements, classification rules, endpoint updates, single-transition restriction and stopping limits.
The bounded localization claim is supported under its explicit conditions; no additional unresolved empirical relation is needed.

rationale: With valid endpoints, comparable trials and a persistent single transition, each decisive midpoint classification excludes the portion of history incompatible with that transition while preserving its location in the remaining interval. Repetition therefore licenses localization to the final boundary at the stated evidential confidence. The claim establishes association, without asserting sole causation or deployment safety.
uncertainty: Statistical classification uncertainty remains governed by the prespecified evidence and repeated-testing rules. If further classification is infeasible, localization remains an unresolved interval, as explicitly allowed by P015.
